title: Historical Perspective and Further Reading
summary: Work through Historical Perspective and Further Reading.

blocks.md: This lesson follows **Historical Perspective and Further Reading** in *Agent Security* (Vol III).

blocks.source: Vol III, Agent Security, § Historical Perspective and Further Reading
blocks.md: The problem of a program misusing ambient authority on behalf of an untrusted request predates language models by half a century. In a foundational 1972 planning study for the U.S. Air Force, Anderson introduced the concept of the reference monitor, a tamper-proof, universally invoked validation mechanism through which every resource access must pass. Three years later, Saltzer and Schroeder articulated the enduring design principles of protected computer systems, establishing complete mediation, least privilege, and fail-safe defaults as prerequisites for dependable software.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Structural prompt injection matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Instructions, tool definitions, the request, and every observation are serialized into one token sequence in which no position carries enforced privilege, so injection is structural and exposure grows with every untrusted read.

questions.q: The section **Historical Perspective and Further Reading** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Instructions, tool definitions, the request, and every observation are serialized into one token sequence in which no position carries enforced privilege, so injection is structural and exposure grows with every untrusted read.
Confidentiality and integrity provenance vary independently, so the host attaches both to every record, propagates them by the lattice join, and checks release and evidence before dispatch.
A defense is evaluated by system effects at the protected sink on whole eligible episodes, not by model text, and its overhead is priced in cost per accepted task.

Human approval binds to a digest of the canonical, host-resolved action, is presented out of band with the agent's explanation labeled untrusted, and is re-verified with its preconditions immediately before dispatch.

questions.explanation: This section develops **Structural prompt injection**: Instructions, tool definitions, the request, and every observation are serialized into one token sequence in which no position carries enforced privilege, so injection is structural and exposure grows with every untrusted read.

questions.q: True or false: in the book's concept map, *Structural prompt injection* can exploit excess authority prevented by *Complete mediation*.
questions.hint: Which later concept does this idea actually connect to?
questions.explanation: False. The book links *Structural prompt injection* can exploit excess authority prevented by *Callable is not permitted*.
